plan.summary: This 4-week block starts a 12-week off-camp build for boxing with one 60-minute session per week. Week 1 establishes a simple strength baseline with a lower-body multi-rep assessment, then Weeks 2-4 build basic strength, power, trunk stiffness, and boxing-friendly conditioning using bodyweight-only work. With only one S&C session each week, the plan keeps the work focused and recoverable while supporting skill practice. Review progress at the end of Week 4 before the next block.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general strength, jumping power, trunk control, and repeat-effort conditioning with simple bodyweight work.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress unilateral strength and power output while keeping conditioning supportive and recoverable.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Turn the earlier strength work into sharper, faster boxing-relevant movement without forcing a fight-camp peak.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as you can with a quick dip and a quiet landing. Reset between reps so every jump stays sharp.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the countermovement jump feels uncoordinated. Start from a still quarter squat and explode up.

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up with a few easy sets, then work up to your hardest clean set of 3-5 reps per side using a controlled bodyweight tempo. Stop before form breaks and log the reps and tempo quality so this can set your starting baseline.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then perform one hardest clean set of 3-5 reps per side with controlled bodyweight tempo. Log the reps and how solid the set felt so the app can use this as your starting strength baseline.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your best clean set per side and aim to improve control, depth, and stability over time.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if a rear-foot-elevated setup is not practical. Keep the same slow lowering and full range.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Keep the body straight, lower under control, and drive up fast. Stop with 1-2 clean reps left.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use hands on a bench, box, or sturdy surface if full push-ups are not yet clean.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.notes: Make a straight line from head to heel and keep the ribs down. Do not let the hips sag.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if side planks irritate the shoulder. Brace hard and keep the body straight.

exercises.name: Mountain Climber Intervals
exercises.notes: Move fast but stay in control. Keep the hips steady and shoulders stacked over the hands.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump high, land softly, and fully reset between reps. Stop if height clearly drops.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the countermovement jump still feels inconsistent. Keep each rep crisp.

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use a 3-second lower, brief pause, then stand up hard. Keep balance and full foot pressure through the front leg.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your strongest clean set each side and add reps or better control before adding difficulty.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the elevated version is awkward or unstable. Keep the same tempo and depth.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Lower under control and press up with speed. Keep 1-2 clean reps in reserve.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Raise the hands enough to keep all reps crisp and full range.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a 3-second lower if regular push-ups are too easy without extra load.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Drive through the heel and finish with the hips fully extended. Do not arch the low back.

substitutionOptions.name: Glute Bridge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use two legs if single-leg work causes cramping or loss of pelvic control.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Keep the low back gently pressed down and the ribs tucked. Shorten the lever if you lose position.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the hollow hold is too difficult to keep clean.

exercises.name: Burpee Intervals
exercises.notes: Keep the pace honest but smooth. Land softly and keep the reps consistent across rounds.

exercises.name: Skater Jump to Stick
exercises.notes: Jump side to side, land balanced, and hold each landing for a moment. Stay springy but controlled.

substitutionOptions.name: Lateral Step and Stick
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this lower-impact option if the full skater jump is too unstable.

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use a smooth lower and drive up hard. Keep the front knee tracking over the foot and stay tall through the torso.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your best-quality set each side and build reps with clean depth and balance.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if setup or balance still limits clean work.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Drive up fast on every rep. If you can do all sets easily, slow the lower to keep the work challenging.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Add a 3-second lowering phase if standard reps are too easy.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if clean full-range reps fall below the target.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.notes: Step back long enough to keep the front foot flat and the torso stable. Push through the floor to return.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if reverse lunges feel too wobbly.

exercises.name: Side Plank with Reach
exercises.notes: Reach under with control, then open back up without letting the hips drop. Move slowly and stay braced.

substitutionOptions.name: Side Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use the standard hold if adding the reach reduces position quality.

exercises.name: Shadow Boxing Conditioning Rounds
exercises.notes: Work at a strong but sustainable pace with sharp footwork and clean breathing. Keep the shoulders relaxed and the hands fast.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Keep each rep snappy and stop well before fatigue. This week is about staying fresh while keeping speed.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if it feels easier to keep clean and quick.

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use the same tempo as earlier weeks but cut the effort down a notch. Smooth reps only.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track how easy and stable your best set feels this week. The goal is quality, not fatigue.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want an easier setup for the deload week.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Leave a couple of good reps in reserve and keep the press fast. Do not grind.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need to keep the reps cleaner and easier this week.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Squeeze at the top and keep the pelvis level. Smooth controlled reps only.

substitutionOptions.name: Glute Bridge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use both legs if you want a lighter option this week.

exercises.name: Front Plank
exercises.notes: Brace hard, breathe behind the brace, and keep the body straight. Finish before shaking changes the position.

exercises.name: Shadow Boxing Aerobic Flush
exercises.notes: Keep the pace light and rhythmic. Use this to leave the session feeling better, not drained.
